profile.campus: Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio (CyrusOne CIN2 campus)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility page, CIN2 sits at 229 West 7th St, Cincinnati, OH 45202, a 14-story former telecom carrier hotel (the building previously operated under the Broadwing name, a Cincinnati-based telecommunications company, before CyrusOne's ownership) publishing 143,778 sq ft of technical IT space and 11 MW of IT capacity; CyrusOne describes CIN2 as the city's primary carrier hotel facility, located roughly 15 minutes from Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport, with closed-loop chilled-water cooling with redundant makeup-water feeds and a FEMA priority-list designation.

This facility is part of CyrusOne's Cincinnati-metro cluster, the company's home market: Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry states Cincinnati Bell purchased a stake in CyrusOne for $525 million in 2010 and divested it in 2015 after CyrusOne's 2013 IPO; the company was originally founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it for approximately $15 billion. The Cincinnati cluster spans buildings in Cincinnati proper, Lebanon, and Butler and Warren Counties in Ohio, plus a related facility across the Ohio River in Florence, Kentucky, reflecting the metro's historical role as CyrusOne's founding market before the company's national and international expansion.

Ohio's Cincinnati metro sits within the PJM Interconnection regional transmission grid, and Duke Energy is the dominant electric utility serving the Cincinnati area; PJM has separately flagged rising data center electricity demand across its multi-state footprint (which spans much of the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, including Northern Virginia's much larger concentration of facilities) as a factor in its long-term capacity planning. Cincinnati's relatively central US location, moderate climate, and status as CyrusOne's founding home market, rather than proximity to any single hyperscale anchor tenant, are what have kept the company concentrating multiple buildings in this metro even as its larger growth in recent years has shifted toward Texas, Virginia, and international markets.

reading.body:
CIN2 publishes 11 MW of IT load across 143,778 square feet of technical space, making it Ohio's third-largest published data center campus by capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this represents roughly 275 racks; at 10 kW per GPU, a typical inference density, this could support roughly 1,100 GPUs. The campus ranks third among the eight Ohio facilities that publish power figures, which collectively represent 60.4 MW of the 76 mapped facilities in the state.

The certifications published for CIN2 qualify it to host regulated workloads: HIPAA for health data, PCI DSS for payment systems, FISMA for federal information systems, ISO 27001 for information security, and SSAE 16 Type II for service organization controls. These certifications do not indicate which workloads the campus actually serves.

CIN2 sits in Cincinnati's downtown core at 229 West 7th Street, within the metro cluster that spans Ohio and northern Kentucky. The campus is part of CyrusOne, the operator taken private in 2022 by KKR and GIP for $15 billion. Total IT capacity at the site is too small for the largest AI training clusters, but sufficient for mid-scale inference, model serving, or regulated AI workloads where compliance certifications matter.
